questions.t: Which product are you assessing?
questions.h: Pick exactly one. Run the questionnaire once per product; home loans are split into fixed and variable because their features differ.

o.l: Everyday account
o.n: Maps to the transaction_account product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Savings account
o.n: Maps to the savings_account product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Term deposit
o.n: Maps to the term_deposit product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Credit card
o.n: Maps to the credit_card product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Personal loan
o.n: Maps to the personal_loan product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Home loan (fixed rate)
o.n: Maps to the home_loan_fixed product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

o.l: Home loan (variable rate)
o.n: Maps to the home_loan_variable product tag; other questions are filtered to this product.

questions.t: Through which channels is this product available or serviced?
questions.h: Tick every channel customers can use to open, use or service the product, not only the main one.

o.l: Mobile app
o.n: Maps to the mobile_app channel tag; channel-specific questions are filtered accordingly.

o.l: Internet banking
o.n: Maps to the online_banking channel tag; channel-specific questions are filtered accordingly.

o.l: Phone banking (call centre)
o.n: Maps to the call_centre channel tag; channel-specific questions are filtered accordingly.

o.l: Retail network (branches)
o.n: Maps to the branch channel tag; channel-specific questions are filtered accordingly.

questions.t: Who is this product designed for and open to?
questions.h: Tick every group the product is available to, including through exceptions or special offers. Mass-market individuals are the default.

o.l: Adult individuals generally (mass market)
o.n: Mass-market individuals are the baseline; deliberately no retail tag, because most typologies list retail and it would not discriminate between them.

o.l: Children, teenagers or students (youth or student offers, minor accounts)
o.n: Youth and student offers map to student_youth, a common mule-recruitment and scam-target group.

o.l: Older customers, or customers likely to be vulnerable (seniors offers, carers, customers who rely on others to bank)
o.n: Older and vulnerable customers map to vulnerable_elderly (scams, elder financial abuse).

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Is the product open to customers who live overseas, hold temporary visas, or have links to politically exposed people?
questions.h: Think about eligibility rules and what happens in practice, not just the target market.

o.l: Non-residents, temporary visa holders, or customers with overseas income or addresses
Customers who are, or are related to or closely associated with, politically exposed persons (PEPs)
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Do sole traders or self-employed customers commonly use this personal product for business purposes?
questions.h: Sole traders (self-employed individuals) often run business receipts and payments through personal products, which blurs personal and business activity and weakens business-customer controls.

o.l: Yes, this is common or expected
o.n: Maps to sole_trader (self-employed individual using a personal product for business), replacing the weaker sme tag.

o.l: No, business use is excluded or rare
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers who are new to the bank, or have little or no credit or banking history, open this product?
questions.h: Include customers with a thin file, recent arrivals and customers with no existing relationship.

o.l: Yes, new-to-bank customers can open it, often with limited history
o.n: Maps to new_to_bank (synthetic identity, mule and first-party fraud exposure).

o.l: No, an existing relationship or established history is required
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers send and receive real-time (fast) payments from this account?
questions.h: Real-time payments settle in seconds and cannot be recalled easily, so funds can move out before a scam or mule account is detected.

o.l: Yes, send real-time payments to other people (pay anyone)
Yes, receive real-time payments from other people
o.n: Inbound fast payments also map to fast_payments (mule and scam proceeds).

o.l: Funds can be paid to external accounts in the customer's own name only
o.n: Own-name-only restriction: no rail added beyond the above.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How are limits and controls set for payments to new payees?
questions.h: Look at daily limits, first-payment holds, cooling-off periods and confirmation of payee.

o.l: High or no limits for new payees, funds go immediately
o.n: Weak new-payee friction increases fast-payment exposure.

o.l: Moderate limits with some friction (e.g. lower first-day limit, warning messages)
o.n: Fast payments still available, so rail remains relevant.

o.l: Strict controls (e.g. holds on new payees, step-up authentication, payee name checks)
o.n: Strong controls: assessed by the institution; no extra rail tag.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How can customers put cash in and take cash out of this account?
questions.h: Cash is anonymous and hard to trace. Include ATMs with deposit capability and branch counters.

o.l: Cash deposits at ATMs or intelligent deposit machines
Cash deposits or withdrawals over the branch counter
Cash withdrawals at ATMs or via cash-out at retailers
No cash handling is allowed on this product
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Does this account allow cheques, direct debits or bill payments?
questions.h: Cheques are slow to clear and open to alteration; direct debits can be used to pull funds from unaware third parties; biller-code (BPAY style) payments move value to third-party billers and can be used to settle other people's obligations.

o.l: Cheque deposits or cheque books
Direct debits or recurring batch payments (e.g. regular payment authorities)
Bill payments using biller codes (e.g. BPAY) or bill-pay services
No cheques, direct debits or bill payments
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What cards are linked to this account, and where can they be used?
questions.h: Include debit cards, digital wallet provisioning, and overseas use.

o.l: Debit card for in-store, ATM and online (card-not-present) use
Digital wallets (e.g. phone or watch tap-and-pay)
o.n: Wallet tap-and-pay is a card token, so it maps to card only (stored_value_wallet is reserved for prepaid or stored-value accounts, not in scope).

o.l: Overseas ATM and card use enabled by default or by request
o.n: Overseas card and cash withdrawal map to card and cash.

o.l: No card is linked
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers make international transfers from this account?
questions.h: Include SWIFT transfers, overseas remittance services and foreign-currency payments, in any channel.

o.l: SWIFT or bank-to-bank international transfers
Remittance or money-transfer service, including to high-risk corridors
International transfers not offered
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can the account be held jointly, or can someone else operate it for the customer?
questions.h: Joint holders, power of attorney, authorised signatories and carers all count.

o.l: Joint accounts with any other person (family, friends, unrelated)
o.n: Baseline segment: no tag (retail is not used because it does not discriminate between typologies).

o.l: Power of attorney, guardianship or authorised third-party operators
o.n: Third-party operators map to vulnerable_elderly (financial abuse, coerced access).

o.l: Parent or guardian access to a minor's account
Single holder only, no third-party access
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How are interest or bonus rates structured, and can customers withdraw freely?
questions.h: Bonus rates that depend on deposits or balances can encourage structuring or parking of funds from third parties.

o.l: Bonus interest for monthly deposits or regular transfers into the account
o.n: Deposit-count incentives map to fast_payments and direct_debit_batch (incoming transfers).

o.l: Bonus interest for keeping a minimum balance or no withdrawals
o.n: No rail follows; behaviour-based controls apply.

o.l: High promotional rate that attracts large new money from other institutions
o.n: Large inbound funds map to fast_payments and wire_swift.

o.l: Customers can withdraw any amount at any time with no notice or limit
o.n: Instant unrestricted withdrawal maps to fast_payments and cash.

o.l: Withdrawals are limited by number, amount or notice period, or the rate is flat with no conditions
o.n: Limits reduce pass-through use; no rail tag.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What are the minimum and maximum deposit amounts for this term deposit?
questions.h: Large maximums can be used to place significant funds with a low question-asking threshold. Tick all that apply.

o.l: Large maximum (e.g. above $1 million) or no maximum
o.n: High value placements map to wire_swift and private_wealth.

o.l: Mid-range maximum (e.g. up to a few hundred thousand dollars)
Low minimum (e.g. $1,000 or less) used by many small savers
o.n: Baseline segment: no tag (retail is not used because it does not discriminate between typologies).

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How can a term deposit be funded?
questions.h: Consider the source of the initial lump sum and any top-ups at rollover.

o.l: Transfer from a customer's existing account with the bank
Transfer from an account at another bank or funded by a third party
o.n: Funding from another bank or a third party maps to fast_payments and third_party_funder.

o.l: Cash or cheque deposit at a branch
Funds from overseas
o.n: Overseas funding maps to wire_swift, cross_border_remittance and non_resident.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What happens if a customer wants to break the term deposit early?
questions.h: Early break is the point at which a term deposit becomes liquid again, so early-break rules decide how it could be used to layer funds.

o.l: Allowed with notice and a penalty, but paid out to any account the customer nominates
o.n: Liquid early exit to arbitrary accounts maps to fast_payments and wire_swift.

o.l: Allowed only in exceptional circumstances (hardship, death) and paid to the original account
Not allowed
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Where can maturity proceeds be paid?
questions.h: Third-party and cheque payouts break the link between the customer and the original source of funds.

o.l: To the customer's own account at the same bank only
To an account at another bank in the customer's name
To a third party's account, or to an account in another name
o.n: Third-party payout maps to fast_payments; payouts to other names also hint at intermediary involvement, mapped to professional_intermediary.

o.l: By cheque
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Do term deposits roll over automatically, and can funds be added or the nominated account changed?
questions.h: Automatic rollover with changes to nominated accounts is a common ATO and layering route.

o.l: Automatic rollover with the option to top up
o.n: Top-ups at rollover map to fast_payments and cash.

o.l: Nominated payout account can be changed by phone, online or in branch
o.n: Remote changes map to fast_payments; vulnerable customers are targeted for account takeover.

o.l: Automatic rollover only, no changes without a new application
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can the term deposit be used as security for borrowing?
questions.h: Loans secured on deposits are a classic loan-back route: borrowed funds are paid out while the deposit is broken or liquidated to repay.

o.l: Yes, the bank lends against the deposit (lien or loan against deposit)
o.n: Loan against deposit: loan_disbursement and loan_early_payout.

o.l: Yes, it can secure borrowing by someone else (third party or other lender)
o.n: Deposit securing a third party's borrowing: loan_disbursement and third_party_funder.

o.l: No, the deposit cannot be used as security
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers take cash advances on the credit card?
questions.h: Cash advances move credit into cash and are a known route for fraud proceeds and gambling.

o.l: Cash advance at ATMs or branches
o.n: Cash advances are cash-like credit: cash, card and bnpl_cash_like.

o.l: Cash-like transactions (e.g. gambling, money orders, crypto purchases)
o.n: Cash-like purchases map to card, crypto on/off-ramp and bnpl_cash_like.

o.l: Cash advances and cash-like transactions are blocked
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers transfer balances from other cards or use the card to pay other lenders?
questions.h: Balance transfers and bill-pay can be used to cycle funds between facilities.

o.l: Balance transfers from other credit cards or personal loans
o.n: Balance transfers pay out credit to other lenders: card and loan_disbursement.

o.l: Bill payments (biller codes) or transfers to third-party accounts from the card
o.n: Bill payments or transfers from the card map to bill_payment, card and fast_payments.

o.l: Neither
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What happens when customers overpay or hold a credit balance on the card?
questions.h: Overpayments can be refunded to a different account, creating a "clean" payout.

o.l: Credit balances above the limit are allowed and refunded on request
Refunds are paid to a different account or by cheque
Refunds only go back to the account that made the payment
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Does the card allow additional cardholders, and how are credit limit increases handled?
questions.h: Additional cardholders are often family members; automated limit increases can be used for bust-out.

o.l: Additional cardholders, including under 18s or people unrelated to the primary holder
o.n: Maps to card, student_youth and vulnerable_elderly.

o.l: Credit limit increase available by app, online or phone without full reassessment
o.n: Easy limit increase maps to card and new_to_bank (bust-out fraud).

o.l: Limit increases need a new application and income verification
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Where can the card be used?
questions.h: Consider overseas use, online (card-not-present) use, and digital wallets.

o.l: Overseas in-store and ATM use
Online and phone purchases (card-not-present)
Digital wallets and "buy now pay later" or instalment features
o.n: BNPL and instalment features map to card and bnpl_cash_like.

o.l: Gambling, crypto exchange or other higher-risk merchants not blocked
o.n: Higher-risk and cash-like merchants map to card, crypto and bnpl_cash_like.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What is the loan used for, and is the purpose checked?
questions.h: Unverified or flexible purposes allow loan funds to be used for scam payments, gambling or cash.

o.l: Any purpose, not checked (e.g. cash out, "personal use")
o.n: Unchecked purpose allows cash-out: loan_disbursement, fast_payments and cash.

o.l: Specific purpose (e.g. vehicle, renovation, debt consolidation), checked with invoices or payout to a third party
o.n: Purpose-checked loans still disburse credit, often to a seller or supplier: loan_disbursement.

o.l: Education or travel for customers who are overseas or temporary residents
o.n: Overseas-linked education or travel loans map to loan_disbursement, remittance, non_resident and student_youth.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Is the loan unsecured, or secured on something other than property?
questions.h: Loans secured on cash, term deposits or cars have different loan-back and asset-laundering risks.

o.l: Unsecured
o.n: Unsecured credit is typically paid out by fast payment.

o.l: Secured on a vehicle, boat or other asset
o.n: Asset-secured loans map to wire_swift and private_wealth.

o.l: Secured on cash or a term deposit (including loans against deposits held with the bank)
o.n: Loans against deposits are the loan-back pattern: loan_disbursement, loan_early_payout (repayment by breaking or liquidating the deposit), wire_swift, private_wealth.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How quickly, and to whom, is the money paid out?
questions.h: Fast, direct or third-party payouts leave little time for checks; payout to third parties and cash-out are loan disbursement exposure.

o.l: Same day or instant to the customer's account
o.n: Instant payout to the customer: loan_disbursement and fast_payments.

o.l: Directly to a third party (dealer, builder, conveyancer, settlement agent)
o.n: Third-party payout: loan_disbursement, wire_swift, fast_payments and professional_intermediary.

o.l: By cheque or cash
o.n: Cheque or cash payout: loan_disbursement, cheque and cash.

o.l: Payout only after settlement or document checks (no cash-out)
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers top up the loan or draw more later?
questions.h: Top-ups and redraws increase the cash that can be extracted from existing facilities.

o.l: Yes, top-ups are available and approved quickly, often without a fresh assessment
o.n: Fast top-ups are repeat disbursements: loan_disbursement and fast_payments.

o.l: Top-ups need a full new application
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can the loan be used like a line of credit, or for buy-now-pay-later or point-of-sale finance?
questions.h: Credit that behaves like cash, or that pays merchants directly, is exposed to cash-out and merchant-collusion typologies.

o.l: Point-of-sale, buy-now-pay-later or instalment finance paid direct to retailers
o.n: Merchant-paid and BNPL style credit maps to loan_disbursement and bnpl_cash_like.

o.l: Revolving or redraw-style access to further cash after settlement
o.n: Cash-like credit access maps to loan_disbursement, bnpl_cash_like and cash.

o.l: One-off fixed drawdown only
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers repay early or in lump sums, and who makes repayments?
questions.h: Early and third-party payouts clear the loan quickly and can launder value or hide the true source of funds.

o.l: Lump-sum or early payout allowed without a fee
o.n: Early or lump-sum payout maps to loan_early_payout.

o.l: Repayments in cash at branch or by cheque
Repayments from overseas accounts or by third parties unrelated to the borrower
o.n: Overseas or unrelated third-party repayments: loan_early_payout, wire_swift, remittance, non_resident and third_party_funder.

o.l: Regular repayments paid by a third party or company on the borrower's behalf
o.n: Repayments by a third party or company on the borrower's behalf: loan_early_payout, fast_payments and third_party_funder.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Are loans arranged through brokers, introducers or other third parties?
questions.h: Intermediaries sit between the bank and the customer and can alter or fabricate documents.

o.l: Yes, a large share comes from brokers or introducers
Direct only (branch, phone or online)
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Do guarantors, co-borrowers or other third parties commonly support or fund the loan?
questions.h: Guarantors and third-party funders can be coerced, elderly or acting as a front for the real beneficiary.

o.l: Guarantor required or commonly used (e.g. parents guaranteeing a young borrower)
o.n: Guarantors are a third party funding or backing the borrower: third_party_funder.

o.l: Joint borrowers who are unrelated or recently introduced
o.n: Unrelated or recently introduced joint borrowers map to new_to_bank and third_party_funder.

o.l: Single borrower, no guarantor
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Is the home loan mainly for living in or for investment?
questions.h: Investor lending involves rental income, multiple properties and more complex funding.

o.l: Mostly owner-occupier
o.n: Baseline segment: no tag (retail is not used because it does not discriminate between typologies).

o.l: Mix of owner-occupier and investor lending
Mostly investors, including those with several properties or self-managed funds
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Where does the borrower's deposit come from, and how is it checked?
questions.h: Gifted deposits and deposits from overseas or in cash are a known property laundering route.

o.l: Savings held with the bank for some time
o.n: Baseline segment: no tag (retail is not used because it does not discriminate between typologies).

o.l: Gifted by family or other third parties
o.n: Gifted deposits map to third_party_funder and fast_payments.

o.l: Sent from overseas
o.n: Maps to wire_swift, cross_border_remittance and non_resident.

o.l: Paid in cash or with large cheques
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How is the property valued before lending?
questions.h: Valuations are a control point; broker-chosen or desktop valuations can be manipulated.

o.l: Independent panel valuer chosen by the bank
Valuer or valuation firm nominated by the broker or borrower
Automated or desktop valuations for some loans
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How are fixed-rate locks and break costs handled?
questions.h: Break costs and rate locks affect when and how large lump sums are paid.

o.l: Rate lock available before settlement, often arranged by a broker
Early exit or full payout during the fixed term, subject to a break cost
o.n: Early exit or full payout during the fixed term: loan_early_payout.

o.l: Break costs may be paid by a third party or unrelated account
o.n: Third-party break costs or payout: loan_early_payout, fast_payments, third_party_funder.

o.l: Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Does the loan have an offset account, redraw, or flexible extra repayments?
questions.h: Offsets and redraws let borrowers hold and withdraw large sums, so the loan acts like a transaction account.

o.l: Offset account linked to the loan, accepting deposits from anyone
o.n: Offset accepting deposits from anyone: fast_payments and cash.

o.l: Redraw of extra repayments to any account via app, online or phone
o.n: Redraw to any account is a disbursement of loan funds: loan_disbursement, fast_payments, wire_swift.

o.l: Redraw by cash or cheque at branch
o.n: Redraw by cash or cheque: loan_disbursement, cash, cheque.

o.l: Unlimited extra repayments without fees, or the loan can be split into fixed and variable parts
o.n: Unlimited extra repayments allow rapid payout: loan_early_payout.

o.l: Neither feature, and extra repayments are capped or fee-based
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How are new customers identified and onboarded in the app or online?
questions.h: Remote onboarding relies on document and biometric checks that can be defeated by synthetic or stolen identities.

o.l: Fully remote with electronic ID or document checks and no face-to-face contact
o.n: Maps to new_to_bank (remote onboarding is where synthetic and stolen identities enter).

o.l: Remote onboarding available to non-residents or customers with foreign ID
Customers must verify ID in a branch or by video call with a bank employee
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What controls protect devices and sessions in the app or online?
questions.h: Device and session controls reduce account takeover and remote-access scams.

o.l: A new device or browser can make payments straight away
Customers can share screens or allow remote access without detection
Device binding, one-time codes and session risk checks are applied
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Can customers change contact details, limits or payees remotely?
questions.h: Changing contact details and limits is the first step of most account takeover.

o.l: Change mobile number, email or address in the app, online or by phone
Increase payment or card limits remotely
All changes require extra verification or a branch visit
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: How are customers authenticated, and what can they instruct, by phone?
questions.h: Call-centre social engineering is a common route to account takeover and unauthorised payments.

o.l: Identity verified with personal details only, no one-time code
Phone instructions can include payments, large or international transfers
Customers can be called back or verified with a one-time code
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: What cash handling and ID checks happen at the branch counter?
questions.h: Branch staff see customers, cash and documents directly.

o.l: Cash deposits and withdrawals above reporting thresholds
Third parties depositing cash into customer accounts
Foreign or unfamiliar ID documents accepted
Not sure / not applicable

questions.t: Do customers come to the branch or phone line with someone else who speaks for them?
questions.h: Accompanied customers can signal coercion or exploitation.

o.l: Older or vulnerable customers who are accompanied by others
Young customers or students accompanied by non-family members
Customers new to the bank who are accompanied by an introducer
Not sure / not applicable

profiles.d: Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Mass-market everyday account with real-time payments, debit card and digital wallets, cheques and direct debits, ATM and branch cash, joint and POA access, SWIFT transfers, all four channels.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Bonus-interest online saver linked to an everyday account, real-time transfers in and out, ATM and branch deposits, withdrawal limits, joint holding; app, internet banking and branch.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Fixed-term deposit funded from the customer's own accounts or other banks, early break with penalty to any nominated account, maturity to own or other-bank account, auto-rollover, loans against the deposit; internet banking, phone and branch.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Mass-market credit card with cash advance, balance transfers, additional cardholders, online limit increases, overseas and card-not-present use, digital wallets; all four channels.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Unsecured personal loan with purpose check, same-day payout to the customer, top-ups, early repayment, some broker origination, existing-customer ID checks; app, internet banking and phone.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Mostly owner-occupier home loan, broker-originated, gifted deposits, settlement to conveyancer, fixed-term break costs, lump-sum exit; internet banking, phone and branch.

Illustrative only, not an assessment of any real product. Mostly owner-occupier variable loan with offset account, redraw, unlimited extra repayments, broker-originated, savings-funded deposit; all four channels.
